title: Four Forearm Routines - Larry Scott
author: Mithosphere
desc:
INTRODUCTION
Although the biceps are the most popular of all the muscles on the male physique, they have a close rival. It is hard to find a muscle with more impact on the eye than a mighty forearm laced with deep blue veins.

Over the years my forearms have grown and now provide me with a real sense of satisfaction. Probably even more so than the upper arm because they are always in view, even in a short sleeve shirt. The following routines will do the same for yours if you diligently apply yourself to the advice I am about to give you.

GENERAL INFORMATION
These routines are not designed for the beginner. They are painful, gut-busting, tough routines, designed to build big forearms. I know it can be done using these very exercises because I have done it. However, it does not happen overnight. Forearms are difficult, stubborn, and training them is downright painful, but it is a sweet pain and one that is endurable.

If you are just beginning to consider training the forearms to build wrist wrestling power, I suggest you ease into it. If 3 or 4 series are suggested, you may want to do only 1 or 2 until you get used to it.

EQUIPMENT NEEDED
Olympic bar and plates
Barbell
Preacher bench
Lat machine
EZ curl bar
Preacher bench curling machine
Dumbbells
Wrist roller
Wrist curling bench

Here is the key to building good forearms. Design a sturdy bench about 16 inches high and one foot square. Pad it with high density foam, about one inch thick and give very little when used. The dimensions are important. You can get your knees around a one foot bench and drop your rear end down low to get your guts into the exercise when the reps get hard.

16 inches high is just perfect to keep the 45 lb. Olympic plates from hitting the floor, and just high enough to almost pry the bar up off the floor on the first rep with the back of the forearms against the bench.

IN CLOSING
I've given you some of the toughest routines of which I am aware. I have purposely tried to give you the hardest ones so that you can gradually grow into it. Forearm training can be really exciting. Feel free to pick and choose exercises from one routine to another. You may hit on something that works better than I have.

Good luck to you and remember - always warm up before a session!

ex.note: Use light weight. Let the bar roll all the way down to the end of the fingers on some of the reps. Rest 1-2 minutes before moving to next exercise.

ss.note: Heavy, with thumbs under bar. Do not let bar roll into fingers. Try to get 20 reps - this is your POWER movement.
Use light weight. Let the bar roll all the way down to the fingertips for all reps.
Do one set of 6 reps and drop the weight and repeat another set; drop the weight once more and complete last set. No rest at all between sets.
